testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light on the dashboard means the ABS (anti-lock braking system) is not working properly.

questions.question: If you have more than one driver's license:

options.text: You likely will not be caught.
You may be caught because states share information through computers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be caught because states share information through computers.
questions.explanation: All states share driver information using a computer database. This prevents people from getting more than one driver's license. Having multiple licenses is illegal.

questions.question: Lights that show anti-lock brakes are not working are:
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS (anti-lock braking systems) have a yellow warning light that shows when there is a problem with the brakes.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you would check and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would check and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must tell the examiner what you are checking and why you are checking it.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during a vehicle inspection:

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at slower speeds.
The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
The vehicle is fine to drive because most of the spring is still there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: When checking a vehicle's suspension, look for broken or missing leaves in the leaf springs. Missing one-fourth or more leaves is dangerous and puts the vehicle out of service.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, missing exits, drifting from your lane, and feeling restless. Staying in your lane is a sign of safe driving, not fatigue.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. A leak in one system might not affect the other system.

questions.question: Bridges usually freeze:

options.text: Only when temperatures are well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.

questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be careful on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not be provoked by angry gestures from another driver. Avoid eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: While driving:

options.text: Creating a text is not allowed, but reading one is.
Creating a text is allowed, but reading one is not.
Creating and reading texts are both not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Creating and reading texts are both not allowed.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is illegal. This includes typing text and reading text on an electronic device.

questions.question: What should you do with broken suspension parts?

options.text: Fix them, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous and must be fixed immediately.

questions.question: What information does NOT need to be included in an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the trip dates and total distance traveled. It does not need to include the number of vehicles passed.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, how many seconds should it take for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi in both tanks. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When drivers turn, which way do they usually look?

options.text: In the direction of the turn.
In the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Drivers usually look in the direction they are turning. If a driver does not signal, their body movements may still show they are about to turn.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, when do you receive points against your score?

options.text: When you cross over exercise boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you cross over exercise boundaries.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each touch or crossing counts as an error.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems make too much noise.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding causes the most deaths and injuries in work zones. Be extra careful when driving near workers.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first begins to fall?

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, it mixes with oil drippings that are still on the road. This creates a very slippery surface.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of aggressive driving?

options.text: You expect delays on your drive.
You slow down and keep a safe distance from other cars.
You make hand gestures that anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You make hand gestures that anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Do not be an aggressive driver. Allow extra time for your trip, keep a safe distance, and never make angry hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: Who is responsible for making sure cargo on a truck is secure?

options.text: The person who loaded the truck

questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for checking the cargo and making sure it is properly secured, even if someone else loaded it.

questions.question: What is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver does not show up for their scheduled basic skills test.
A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
A driver fails one part of the basic skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle touches a boundary line during the basic skills test.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the basic skills test. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: When you inspect a fifth wheel, what should you check?

options.text: Make sure the locking jaws are open.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Check that the fifth wheel locking jaws are closed tightly around the kingpin. They should grip the kingpin shaft, not the head.

questions.question: In cold weather, when do bridges freeze?

options.text: After other parts of the road.
Before other parts of the road.
At the same time as other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. Be extra careful on bridges and overpasses when it is wet and cold.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When you stop at a traffic signal

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before each trip. If you have a trailer, it should be straight when you adjust your mirrors.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a header board?

options.text: They protect drivers from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
They protect drivers' heads when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect drivers from cargo that shifts during a crash or sudden stop.
questions.explanation: A header board protects the driver from cargo moving forward during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: When are containerized loads used?

options.text: When cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
When cargo has been or will be transported by train.

questions.correctAnswerText: When cargo has been or will be transported by train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight travels partly by train or ship. You cannot inspect sealed containers, but you must make sure they do not exceed safe weight limits.

questions.question: What does it mean if the safety relief valve is releasing air?

options.text: This is normal and not a concern.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if system pressure gets too high. If it releases air, there is a problem. Have a mechanic inspect and fix the brakes.

questions.question: When braking on a downhill slope, what speed should you reach?
questions.explanation: On a downhill slope, brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process as needed.

questions.question: What can rust around wheel nuts indicate?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check that the nuts are tight if you see rust.

questions.question: What should you do if your brakes fail going downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down by itself.
Use rumble strips to slow down.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, find an escape ramp quickly to stop your vehicle. If no escape ramp is available, look for an open field or side road that goes uphill or flattens out.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to operate a CMV in intrastate commerce?
questions.explanation: You must be at least 21 years old to drive a CMV across state lines. You can be 18 years old to drive a CMV only within Michigan.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:
questions.explanation: Cargo that is not balanced well can make a vehicle hard to handle. Load cargo with proper weight distribution.

questions.question: When pulled over to the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Rely on your taillights to alert other motorists to your presence.
Use your four-way emergency flashers to alert other motorists to your presence.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way emergency flashers to alert other motorists to your presence.
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when stopped on the side of the road. This is especially important in low visibility. Set warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: Slow down and be extra careful:
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful in work zones, where the road edge drops off, when objects are on the road, and on freeway on- and off-ramps.

questions.question: Loading weight with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Increases the likelihood of a rollover.
Increases the likelihood that items will fall down.
Increases the difficulty of unloading the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the likelihood of a rollover.
questions.explanation: Cargo loaded with a high center of gravity increases the risk that the vehicle will tip over. Always load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: Water that has collected on a roadway can cause:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, check power steering hoses for:

options.text: Extra hose pieces available for repairs.

questions.explanation: Check the power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level during a pre-trip inspection. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: Which is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Tread of 3/32 of an inch in the grooves of the front tires

questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 of an inch of tread depth. Other tires must have at least 2/32 of an inch of tread depth. All tires on the same vehicle must be the same size.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer, turning toward the driver's side is encouraged because:

options.text: The driver will have the best possible view.
Power lines should be on the passenger's side.
Other drivers can offer assistance on the passenger's side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver will have the best possible view.
questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's left side. This gives the driver the best view of the rear of the vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement about driver licenses is correct?

options.text: You can have more than one license if one is for business purposes.
You can have more than one license if they are from different states.
You cannot have more than one license.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot have more than one license.
questions.explanation: You can only have one driver license at a time. States share information through a computer system to prevent people from having multiple licenses. Breaking this law can result in fines or jail time.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Hope the vehicle is okay until another driver takes over.
Check it out to find the right solution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it out to find the right solution.
questions.explanation: If you notice, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, you should have it checked.

questions.question: When you apply the brakes, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle should pull to one side.
The vehicle should not pull to either side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should not pull to either side.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, there may be a problem with your brakes.

questions.question: Which surface is the most slippery?
questions.explanation: Wet ice forms when the weather is warm enough to melt ice slightly. Wet ice is much more slippery than dry ice.

questions.question: Before a trip, what should you check about your pedals?

options.text: The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The grooved pedal surface is not worn smooth.
questions.explanation: Before your trip, make sure nothing is blocking the pedals and they work properly. The pedal surfaces should still have their grooves to prevent slipping.

questions.question: What will you be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Explain why you are checking each item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain why you are checking each item.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must complete a full inspection of your vehicle and explain what you are checking and why.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. Parking violations are not included.

questions.question: How can you stop a vehicle from rolling backward when starting to move forward?
questions.explanation: For a manual transmission vehicle, you can prevent rollback by partly engaging the clutch before releasing the brake pedal.

questions.question: How should you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first, then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What does an S-cam do when it turns inside a brake drum?

options.text: It presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
It presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
It presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This friction slows the vehicle.
